rules.action_preference: Take the sign of a trick's value from the contract and keep RAMI and NOLO on separate rule branches. The deal-point scale is exposed as +4 per trick for a RAMI declaring team, +8 for a RAMI defending partnership above the sixth trick, and -4 in NOLO. No policy may use one undifferentiated trick reward.
rules.condition: A policy compares candidate cards by trick value.
rules.limitations: Marginal values are exact only away from the 6/7 boundary, where the swing is larger than one increment.
rules.rationale: The scoring formulas award 4*(declarer tricks - 6), 8*(defender tricks - 6) and 4*(7 - fewer tricks); the sign and the scale genuinely differ.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Consider only the actions present in PlayerObservation.legal_actions, in the engine's stable order.
rules.condition: A policy is asked for an action.
rules.limitations: None; this is a restatement of the rules.
rules.rationale: The engine rejects illegal actions and never repairs them, so the legal set is the whole action space.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Select the lexicographic maximum score vector; break ties by the lowest engine legal-action index.
rules.condition: More than one legal action remains after scoring.
rules.limitations: The tie-break is arbitrary with respect to strength; it is chosen only for reproducibility.
rules.rationale: A single documented tie-break makes the policy reproducible without depending on set iteration or object identity.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Show only a card allowed by project_target_v1 valid_show_cards; accept the derived verbal_required flag.
rules.condition: A policy declares a contract during showing.
rules.limitations: project_target_v1 has no cardless verbal declaration, so the legacy 'declare with no card' branch cannot be reproduced.
rules.rationale: project_target_v1 restricts show ranks to 3-9 and defines an explicit off-colour and no-eligible-rank fallback hierarchy.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Prefer to shed a card that is the highest unplayed card of its suit.
rules.condition: The policy may discard or safely lose in a NOLO deal.
rules.limitations: Shedding a top card can also strip a suit and force later wins elsewhere.
rules.rationale: A card that no unplayed card can beat is a guaranteed future trick, which is exactly what a misere contract must avoid.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Among the lowest-rank candidates, prefer the card with the most unaccounted higher cards in its suit.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead in a NOLO deal.
rules.limitations: A count is not a probability; the rule makes no claim about how those cards are distributed.
rules.rationale: The count of unaccounted higher cards is a hard public count, and a larger count means more cards that can take the trick instead of the leader.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Prefer the cheapest such certain winner over a merely provisional winner.
rules.condition: The policy is following, an opponent holds the trick, and some legal card beats every led-suit card the remaining seats could still hold.
rules.limitations: Only as strong as the public record: an unaccounted higher card blocks the deduction even when nobody actually holds it.
rules.rationale: Hard public inference proves that no remaining seat can hold a higher card of the led suit, so the trick cannot be taken back.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Prefer leading that card.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead and holds the highest unplayed card of some suit.
rules.limitations: Certain for this trick only; it says nothing about who leads the next one or about the rest of the deal.
rules.rationale: project_target_v1 has no trump suit and only led-suit cards can win, so the highest unplayed card of a suit wins with certainty when it is led.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Treat the trick as already conceded by the partnership and discard the highest-liability legal card.
rules.condition: A partner holds the trick in a NOLO deal and no seat still to play can beat the partner's card.
rules.limitations: Ignores that taking the trick oneself would change who leads the next trick.
rules.rationale: NOLO scores team trick totals, so once the partnership is certain to take the trick the choice of card cannot change the team count. Individual trick counts are not scored.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Prefer leading a suit the partner is publicly void in.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead in a NOLO deal and the partner is publicly void in a candidate suit.
rules.limitations: Only voids proven by a public failure to follow are used, so the rule is silent early in a deal.
rules.rationale: A void partner cannot be forced to win that trick and can discard a liability instead.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Overtake with the cheapest certain winner.
rules.condition: A partner holds the trick, a seat still to play could beat it, and the policy holds a card that beats every such card.
rules.limitations: Spends a high card on a trick the partner might have won anyway, and the deduction ignores how likely that is.
rules.rationale: Converting a beatable partner winner into an unbeatable one secures a trick the partnership would otherwise risk.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Avoid leading a suit the partner is publicly void in.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead in a RAMI deal and the partner is publicly void in some candidate suit.
rules.limitations: A void partner can also discard usefully; the rule is a weak preference only.
rules.rationale: A void partner cannot support the suit, so the lead is worth less to the partnership.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Never overtake; play the lowest legal card.
rules.condition: A partner holds the trick and no seat still to play can beat the partner's card.
rules.limitations: Certainty depends on the public record; unaccounted higher cards defeat the deduction.
rules.rationale: The partnership is certain to take the trick, so any card spent on it is pure loss.
rules.validation_status: mechanical consequence of the ruleset

rules.action_preference: Discard the highest-liability card by the ported liability table, preferring short suits on ties.
rules.condition: The policy cannot follow the led suit in a NOLO deal.
rules.limitations: The liability weights are uncalibrated legacy constants.
rules.rationale: Ported from the frozen discard routine: aces and kings are the cards most likely to be forced to win a later trick.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Play the highest such card when last to play, otherwise the lowest.
rules.condition: Every legal card would currently take the trick.
rules.limitations: The earlier-seat branch relies on an opponent or the partner actually overtaking.
rules.rationale: Ported from the frozen policy: the last seat cannot be overtaken, so it purges its largest liability; an earlier seat keeps the trick cheap so a later seat can still take it.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Lead the lowest rank available; break rank ties toward the shortest own suit, then canonical suit order.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead in a NOLO deal.
rules.limitations: Creating a void can also force the partnership to win later tricks in other suits.
rules.rationale: A low lead is unlikely to win the trick, and shortening a suit creates a void that lets the hand discard liabilities later.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Prefer a card that cannot take the trick, and among those the highest, shedding the largest safe liability.
rules.condition: At least one legal card cannot take the current trick.
rules.limitations: Safety is provisional for any seat that is not last to play.
rules.rationale: In a misere contract a trick is a penalty, and a card that is safe now may be a forced winner later.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Prefer a card that does not take the trick from the partner, and among those prefer the lowest.
rules.condition: A partner currently holds the trick in a RAMI deal.
rules.limitations: Provisional: a later opponent may still overtake the partner, and this rule does not look at who is still to play.
rules.rationale: The partnership already holds the trick, so spending a higher card on it cannot add a trick.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Play the cheapest legal card that currently takes it.
rules.condition: An opponent currently holds the trick in a RAMI deal.
rules.limitations: Provisional for any seat that is not last to play; the trick can still be taken back.
rules.rationale: Winning with the cheapest sufficient card preserves strength.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Score each own suit as its high-card weight plus the configured length bonus times its length, then lead the highest card of the best-scoring suit.
rules.condition: The policy is on lead in a RAMI deal.
rules.limitations: Ignores entries, opponent distribution and the value of keeping a high card for a later round. The weight is uncalibrated.
rules.rationale: With no trump suit, top cards and length are the two ordinary sources of tricks; the length bonus makes their trade-off an explicit, ablatable profile weight.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Play the lowest legal card.
rules.condition: No legal card currently takes the trick in a RAMI deal.
rules.limitations: Ignores discard signalling and future suit control.
rules.rationale: A trick that cannot be won should cost as little as possible.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Show the lowest eligible rank of the contract colour; break rank ties by canonical project_target_v1 suit order.
rules.condition: The simple showing profile has chosen a contract.
rules.limitations: Whether minimum-information showing is actually best in this ruleset is untested.
rules.rationale: Revealing the lowest legal card gives an opponent the least usable information about the rest of the hand.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Withhold the RAMI declaration when the NOLO suitability score exceeds the configured veto threshold.
rules.condition: The simple showing profile would otherwise declare RAMI.
rules.limitations: Both thresholds are uncalibrated.
rules.rationale: A hand can be strong in high cards and still be a much better NOLO hand; two explicit thresholds avoid comparing two differently scaled scores.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation

rules.action_preference: Declare RAMI only when high-card points plus ace, control and length bonuses reach the configured threshold.
rules.condition: A policy using the simple showing profile must declare.
rules.limitations: The threshold is uncalibrated and is not claimed to be optimal or even good.
rules.rationale: A small, readable set of hand descriptors is easier to ablate than a calibrated formula and gives an honest floor.
rules.validation_status: UNVALIDATED - no expert or simulation validation
